summary: The producer of the recon slot object and of [recon+DE8h]. 008053C0 lazily allocates a 12A0h object per party into the three-entry table at 00F874BC and constructs it with 008050E0; 008073C0 clears, fills and drains the enemy triple at +0DE4h within one call, so the field a consumer reads holds only records whose detection level is 2. The element is a 0Ch node {prev, next, payload} whose payload is the 1Ch entry record with the unit at +4h.
evidence_kind: static, read-only Ghidra and disk-byte reading. No Ghidra mutation. No run-time evidence: bsp_game.exe builds no recon slot object, which is the gap this packet scopes. The sensor row values quoted in the effect prediction are inherited from docs/SENSOR_TABLE_DATA.md, read from the installed (modded, BSPRM/AlterBSP) arcade table scripts/datatables/classtables/arcade/reconclasses.lua, mtime 2024-07-13 08:26.

host_prescription_note: bsp/recon_slot_lists.hpp already declares the whole rebuild as a pure-virtual host interface and bsp/fixed_step_countdown.hpp already declares the slot table, count, size and offsets. No new header is published by this packet. The only constants found here that no header carries are the {count, head, tail} / {prev, next, payload} strides and the 1Ch record's field offsets; they belong next to kReconTripleOffsets in bsp/recon_slot_lists.hpp, which this packet does not own. recon_contact_count_008053c0 and recon_contact(int) keep their signatures, so src/unit_gunnery_pass.cpp:394 needs no change.

effect_prediction.mechanism: Almost every authored Gain is 1, stored as +8h = 0.5; the rebuild period is 3 s, so one pass contributes 1.5, clamped to cap - current. A vision row's MaxLevel 2 maps to a cap of 1.0f and the identify threshold is 0.5f, so a fresh record saturates to identified in ONE pass. Rule (c) therefore degenerates to a hard range test, with no ramp.
effect_prediction.gating_distance: the vision row, Dist = 4000 m arcade (this installation, GameMode = 0), measured horizontally, times sqrt(rangeScale)
effect_prediction.radar_does_not_qualify: the radar ship's Surface->Surface radar row has Dist 6000 but MaxLevel 1, a cap of 0.25f, and 0.25 is blip not identified (recon_detection_level_00805b3d: < 0.5 is blip). A 4000-6000 m contact is copied into unknown and REMOVED from enemy, so the gunnery sweep never sees it.
effect_prediction.prediction: candidates should be exactly ZERO while the fleets are more than about 4 km apart, then jump to near the stand-in's value once the gap closes, because a task force is a formation a few hundred metres across and the admission envelope is the union over all own-party observers. The run total should fall by roughly the fraction of the run spent beyond the ring, not by a fraction reflecting how many units exist. recon_sweeps does not move: the sweep still runs, its inner loop just has nothing to iterate.
effect_prediction.honest_bound_for_usn02: docs/GAME_EXECUTABLE.md milestone 2s records the nearest enemy pair at 1854 m at 25 s, already well inside 4000 m, so on that mission the closing happens early and the zero stretch is short. The prediction for that run is that candidates moves COMPARATIVELY LITTLE - a reduction concentrated in the opening seconds plus whatever stragglers stay outside the ring.
effect_prediction.falsifier: log, per sweep, the contact count together with the minimum own-to-enemy horizontal distance. The prediction is wrong if the count is a smooth function of time rather than a step at the 4000 m crossing; it is wrong the other way if the count stays at zero after the fleets close, which would mean the observer side of 00806840 finds no rows. A run total alone cannot distinguish 'the filter works' from 'the filter admits nothing'.
